name: Cultural liberalism
scope: Cultural liberalism as political science uses the term: a cluster of attitudes that reject traditional values in the name of individual autonomy, coined by Grunberg and Schweisguth (France de gauche, vote à droite, on the 1978 survey) and measured since in survey research (Schweisguth's three dimensions: liberalism of mores in family and private life; universalist and humanist values, including welcoming immigrants and rejecting discrimination; and attitudes to authority; Bornschier, and Ananda and Dawson, as support for the goals of the new social movements: peace, gender equality, opposition to racism, minority rights). Bréchon calls the concept composite: the dimensions can be held separately, and many holders also want public order. It includes the Anglophone 'social liberalism' sense of liberal stances on abortion, same-sex marriage and similar moral questions only as these sources describe them. It excludes the economic ideology of social liberalism, economic positions (the sources record none as part of the concept; Tiberj finds the economic trend uncertain), and Mill's and the Stanford/Britannica accounts of liberalism, which never name cultural liberalism.

notes: Looked for sources naming the subject: SEP, Britannica (liberalism, libertarianism), Kubik and a Taylor & Francis chapter were saved but never name cultural liberalism, so they are not cited. Not reached: Tournier 2017 (Brill), Bornschier 2010 (paywalled). No English Wikipedia article exists for Grunberg, Schweisguth or Bornschier, so no key figures or key works are listed (France de gauche, vote à droite is named by one source only). Answers: only positions Bréchon's paper and the two other defining sources state are answered; every economic statement and the rest are null. Earlier answers resting on Wikipedia, Mill and the Stanford entry (none names cultural liberalism) are nulled in each statement's history; those three are kept as s1-s3 only for that history. Themes searched: society, family, sexuality, race, immigration, authority, economy (nothing stated).
